content.comment_body: Hello! Could someone assist me? I need to transfer a counter value from one [product_name] controller to another and display it. I've set up a network project (see attachment), connected the controllers, and assigned memory values, but the project isn't working. I'm testing with the simulation feature since I don't have physical controllers.
It appears your project is corrupted. I can open it, but accessing the diagrams only results in an error.
I'll try saving again since I'm not experiencing any issues.

I downloaded your ZIP, extracted it, and opened the project with [product_name] software version [version_no]. It shows two [product_name] controllers in the network view, but attempting to access the diagrams triggers an error message.
Could you please try opening it?
Are you using special characters or a language specific to your country in the diagram names? That might be causing the issue.
Can I upload some screenshots of the project? It's small.
I've checked—I'm not using any unique characters in names.
I think there are special characters in your diagram names. Unfortunately, I can't work with your screenshot because I can't read your language.
I've changed the language in the software, renamed the diagrams, and saved again. Please try now.
I've created a sample for you. Test it out. Note that it doesn't work in simulation—only with physical [product_name] controllers.
Thank you! My setup looks similar, but I wasn't aware data transfer doesn't function in simulation. I'll check it with actual controllers as soon as possible.

Your project is now workable, but there's one more step. You need to use Parameter VM Mapping on both [product_name] controllers, specifically between [product_name][version_no]_1 and [product_name][version_no]_2, in the connection.
Thanks for clarifying. I managed to transfer Flag values between two [product_name] controllers in simulation, so I thought counter values would work in a similar way. I'll keep that in mind.

I used to think the same. Sadly, some functions don't operate in simulation mode. It's unfortunate that [company_name] does not clarify which features are unavailable in simulation. I have also scrapped several project ideas because they failed to work in simulation until I realized the difference when testing with real controllers.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants face challenges opening and editing a [product_name] project designed to simulate data transfer between two controllers. The main issue is an error message when accessing diagrams, which may be related to language or character usage. This highlights problems with project compatibility and localization within simulation mode.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to successfully simulate data transfer between controllers and for project files to be accessible and editable by collaborators, independent of their language or regional settings.
